mechanism: Sub-30 EUR battery sensor (ESP32 + SHT4x) in the bedroom of an at-risk resident. Reports indoor Tmax/Tmin over LoRaWAN or the household router. Crossing a night threshold (e.g. indoor Tmin > 26 C for 2 nights) triggers an automated welfare call from the municipality, not just a push notification.
expected_effect: Converts a population-level forecast into a person-level trigger. Targets the room where most heat deaths occur.
evidence_strength: Medium - components proven; end-to-end escalation loop rarely evaluated
failure_modes: Alert fatigue; false positives in unoccupied rooms; battery neglect; requires a human on the other end of the call

mechanism: Use existing 15-minute smart-meter data already collected by DSOs. A household with no cooling load signature during a heatwave, in a dwelling flagged as poor thermal quality, with an occupant over 75, is a priority visit. No new hardware.
who_deploys: DSO plus municipal social services under a data agreement
expected_effect: Identifies non-cooling households at scale for the price of a query. Uses infrastructure already paid for.
evidence_strength: Medium - the signal is well established in load-disaggregation literature; the public-health application is largely untested
failure_modes: Data-protection approval is the whole project; false negatives for households that cool by shading; requires DSO cooperation

mechanism: Free service that tells a household the exact hour to open and close windows, computed from measured indoor temperature (S1 sensor or a manual reading) and the local outdoor forecast. Delivered by SMS so it works without a smartphone.
expected_effect: Night ventilation is one of the few cooling measures with zero marginal cost and a measurable effect on indoor Tmin in Mediterranean building stock.
evidence_strength: Medium-high for the physics; low for delivery-channel effectiveness
failure_modes: Security concerns prevent window-opening at night in some neighbourhoods; noise and air pollution; no benefit when outdoor Tmin stays above indoor

mechanism: Prioritise external shading (rolling shutters, external blinds, awnings) and reflective roof coatings over deep envelope retrofits or AC subsidies. External shading blocks solar gain before it enters; internal blinds do not. Instrument a sample with S1 sensors to measure the actual effect.
expected_effect: External solar protection is the highest-effect low-cost intervention on Mediterranean summer indoor temperature.
evidence_strength: High for the building physics; medium for population-scale deployment
failure_modes: Heritage and facade restrictions; landlord-tenant split incentive in rental stock; poor installation quality

gap_closed: Intra-urban heat partially mapped but unused
mechanism: Combine free Landsat/Sentinel-3 thermal imagery, Copernicus Urban Atlas tree cover, and OpenStreetMap building footprints to compute shaded walking routes and publish them in the municipal routing app. Pure software on open inputs.
expected_effect: Reduces exposure during unavoidable daytime movement for people without cars.
evidence_strength: Medium - the mapping method is mature; behavioural uptake is the uncertainty
failure_modes: Surface temperature is not the same as felt temperature; routes must be validated on the ground; maintenance after the grant ends

solution: Opportunistic mobile sensing on public fleets
mechanism: Mount a shielded temperature sensor on buses, trams and municipal waste vehicles. A 60-vehicle bus fleet covers more street kilometres per day than any static network a small city could afford.
expected_effect: Dense spatial coverage of street-level air temperature at roughly one percent of the cost of an equivalent static network.
evidence_strength: Medium - demonstrated in research deployments; rarely operationalised
failure_modes: Radiative heating of the sensor while stationary; engine heat contamination; route bias toward main roads

gap_closed: Low-cost networks not comparable or trusted
mechanism: A regional reference station where any citizen or municipal sensor can be co-located for two weeks before and after deployment, returning a calibration certificate and correction coefficients. Solves the quality problem that keeps cheap networks out of official use.
expected_effect: Turns thousands of existing hobbyist sensors into usable public data. Highest leverage per euro of anything in this list.
evidence_strength: High - co-location calibration is the established method and the European street-level compilation shows the interoperability need
failure_modes: Requires an institutional home that outlives project funding; drift between calibrations

solution: Open heat-data schema and municipal API
gap_closed: Networks are non-interoperable; data dies with the project
mechanism: A minimal published schema (station id, lat, lon, height, shielding type, timestamp, temperature, humidity, calibration reference) that any city network must emit. Modelled on the ENTSO-E transparency platform, which made European electricity data usable.
expected_effect: Prevents the recurring pattern where every city network is a bespoke silo that must be harmonised retrospectively.
evidence_strength: High by analogy with ENTSO-E and the 2026 street-level compilation effort
failure_modes: Standards without a mandate are ignored; needs a procurement hook to gain adoption

gap_closed: Vulnerability data not linked to hazard data
mechanism: Pre-agreed roster linking the national heat warning feed to a call list of registered at-risk residents, with volunteers or social workers assigned in advance. The technology is a spreadsheet and an API subscription; the work is the pre-agreement.
expected_effect: Closes the last mile that heat-plan evaluations repeatedly identify as the failure point.
evidence_strength: Medium - plan components are recommended by WHO guidance but evaluation of the individual-contact component is sparse
failure_modes: Consent and data-protection setup; volunteer attrition; register goes stale

solution: Public cool-refuge network with occupancy sensing
mechanism: Designate existing air-conditioned public buildings (libraries, sports halls, shopping centres under agreement) as cool refuges, publish opening hours in the warning feed, and place a 20 EUR people-counter at the door so use is measured and the network can be adjusted.
expected_effect: Uses cooling capacity that already exists and is already paid for, and measures whether anyone actually comes.
evidence_strength: Medium - refuge programmes are widespread; occupancy measurement almost never done
failure_modes: Refuges close at night when tropical nights are the risk; transport barrier for the least mobile; stigma

solution: Carbon-aware scheduling of flexible compute and charging
gap_closed: Grid signal exists but is under-actuated
mechanism: Shift deferrable workloads - model training, batch jobs, EV charging, water heating, building pre-cooling - to hours of low grid carbon intensity using existing free marginal-emissions APIs. Pre-cooling buildings in the cool early morning also cuts peak-hour demand during heatwaves.
expected_effect: Cuts emissions and heatwave peak load without reducing the amount of computation or cooling delivered. The clearest example of solving climate impact without slowing technology.
evidence_strength: High for grid-carbon reduction; medium for the building pre-cooling variant
failure_modes: Requires flexible load; grid carbon signal quality varies by zone; rebound if it enables more total consumption

gap_closed: Adaptation spend not evaluated against measured exposure
mechanism: Mandate that any publicly funded cooling or greening project spends 1-2 percent of budget on before-and-after measurement at the intervention site, with results published to the open schema (S8).
expected_effect: Creates the missing evidence base on what actually reduces exposure per euro, which currently has to be inferred from research pilots.
evidence_strength: High as a method; the gap is institutional not technical
failure_modes: Measurement becomes a compliance box-tick; short measurement windows miss interannual variability
